noHostServing: no wsp host is serving {state}; start one with wsp up --state {state}
hostTokenMissing: the host's token file is missing: {path}
noAnswer: the host at {where} did not answer: {why}
noAnswerWithin: the host at {where} did not answer: nothing came back within {ms} ms
hostStopping: the host is restarting; the turn goes on and its reply lands in the thread
notDelivered: the host stopped before it took the message, so it was not delivered; send it again
noSuchHostNone: no host named {alias} is connected; this computer holds none, and wsp login puts the hosts on your account here. Run wsp hosts for the list.
noSuchHostSome: no host named {alias} is connected; this computer holds {known}, and wsp login puts the hosts on your account here. Run wsp hosts for the list.
severalHosts:
this computer can reach {count} hosts on your account ({aliases}) and none of them is the one every line takes. Name one on the line with --host <name>.

Run wsp hosts for the list.
addressNotPaired: --host takes the name of a host on your account; {url} is an address, and wsp hosts lists the names. Run wsp hosts for the list.
hostNoKey: {where} names a host and no key for it, so this computer cannot tell which host it would be sending its token to; run wsp hosts to read the account's hosts again
launchedWith: the launch this turn started with
deviceRefused: the host {alias} refused this computer's token, which it has taken away; run wsp logout, wsp login and wsp hosts to sign this computer in again.
pairKey: the host at {url} did not prove the key this computer holds for it, so it is not that host; nothing was sent to it
deviceAuthOldHost: the host at {where} runs an older wsp, whose door does not know how a computer on the account comes in; update wsp on that computer and run wsp up there again
scopedNoPair: this thread's tools were launched without its own host token, so they refuse rather than act as the person; the agent did not pass WSP_HOST_URL and WSP_HOST_TOKEN to its MCP server
startingHost: starting the host for {state}; its log is {log}, and wsp down stops it
hostExited: the host for {state} exited with {ended} before it served; its log is {log}

agentNames.build-essential: C toolchain with cmake and ninja

otherVersion: the host answered {op} in a shape this wsp does not read; it runs another version of wsp, restart it with wsp up
aimedUsage: {tool} takes a workspace or on, not both
aimedBoth: A workspace already names its computer; give the workspace or --on <computer>, not both. {usage}
projectUnnamed: --project with --on names the project: --project <name>, as wsp projects shows it. {usage}
projectOffComputer: --project {value} names a project on a computer, which --on names; a workspace's own project is --project alone. {usage}
toolsProjectBare: --project on wsp servers tools names a project on --on <computer>; a workspace finds its own project's servers. {usage}
skillsShPlaceless: {skill} is read off skills.sh, which names no computer or project. {usage}
unsetVariable: {variable} is not set in this environment, so there is no value to write. {usage}
unclosedQuote: The command has a quote it never closes, so nothing was written. {usage}
projectScope: --project is the project scope, not {scope}; give one of the two. {usage}
hostWouldNotRead: the host would not read this line. usage: {usage}

bothTargets.agents: A workspace already names its computer; give the workspace or --on <computer>, not both. agents takes a workspace or on, not both
bothTargets.skills: A workspace already names its computer; give the workspace or --on <computer>, not both. skills takes a workspace or on, not both
bothTargets.servers: A workspace already names its computer; give the workspace or --on <computer>, not both. servers takes a workspace or on, not both

folderHere: folder is a path on this computer, absolute, and got "{path}". Give a path that opens with /, since whoever reads it works in a folder this line cannot see.
folderOn: folder is a path on {name}, absolute, and got "{path}". Give a path that opens with /, since whoever reads it works in a folder this line cannot see.
threadsStartWith: {count} threads start with {ref}; give more of the id
noMessages: thread {thread} has no messages in the transcript this host holds
newerTurn: a newer turn is running; the reply above is the one before it
noTerminalConfig: No Ghostty config on this computer; the terminal pane keeps its defaults.

usages.new: wsp new [<project>] "<what you are working on>" [--size <cpu>x<memGb>] [--engine] [--spawn on|off] [--max-machines <n>] [--max-depth <n>]

workspaces.otherVersionResolve: the host answered workspaces.resolve in a shape this wsp does not read; it runs another version of wsp, restart it with wsp up
workspaces.goneBare: {name}'s machine is gone with its disk, so work that was not pushed is lost; rebuild it to {action}, which brings back its home folder from the last saved nap
workspaces.goneSaid: {name}'s machine is gone with its disk, so work that was not pushed is lost; rebuild it to {action}, which brings back its home folder from the last saved nap ({words})

stateLines.unreachable: {name} is up and not answering yet

rebuildRefused.running: This one is running, so nothing needs rebuilding; the rebuild is offered once a workspace is gone
rebuildRefused.pausing: This one is stopping, so nothing needs rebuilding; the rebuild is offered once a workspace is gone
rebuildRefused.paused: This one is stopped, so nothing needs rebuilding; the rebuild is offered once a workspace is gone
rebuildRefused.waking: This one is waking, so nothing needs rebuilding; the rebuild is offered once a workspace is gone
rebuildRefused.unreachable: This one is not answering yet; the rebuild is offered once it is gone
rebuildRefused.gone: This one is gone, so nothing needs rebuilding; the rebuild is offered once a workspace is gone

workspaces.agentsOne: agents may spawn: up to 1 workspace
workspaces.agentsMany: agents may spawn: up to {count} workspaces
workspaces.agentsNothing: workspaces_agents takes spawn, max_machines or max_depth. Name at least one; with none of them there is nothing to change.
workspaces.forgotOne: forgot {name} {id}: its record and 1 thread are gone from this computer
workspaces.forgotMany: forgot {name} {id}: its record and {count} threads are gone from this computer

cloud.asked: computer is deleted in the cloud
cloud.done: computer {machine} is gone in the cloud

local.asked: computer is left as it is
local.done: its computer is left as it is

copy.asked: copy at {path} is removed and the project folder is left as it is
copy.done: its copy at {path} is removed and the project folder is left as it is

none.asked: create failed before any computer was made, so there is none to delete
none.done: its create had made no computer

workspaces.deleteNoticeOne: Its {asked}; its record and 1 thread leave this computer.
workspaces.deleteNoticeMany: Its {asked}; its record and {count} threads leave this computer.
workspaces.deletedOne: deleted {name} {id}: {done}, and its record and 1 thread are gone from this computer
workspaces.deletedMany: deleted {name} {id}: {done}, and its record and {count} threads are gone from this computer
workspaces.deleteKept: {name} kept. {notice} Ask the person, then call delete again with confirm true.
workspaces.keptFallback: the image it stood on lists no files of its own, so its whole home came across and none of the new image's copies stand
workspaces.keptNone: every file the image wrote came from the new image; none of them had been changed here
workspaces.keptOne: kept 1 changed file: {names}; every other file the image wrote came from the new image
workspaces.keptMany: kept {count} changed files: {names}; every other file the image wrote came from the new image
workspaces.alreadyNewest: already on the newest version of its image, so nothing moved
workspaces.noProjectImage: no project image {id}; wsp image lists them with their ids
workspaces.removeKept: {id} kept. {notice} Ask the person, then call image_remove again with confirm true.
workspaces.removeNotice: Its snapshot, taken from {workspace} on {date}, is deleted at the provider, and no workspace starts from it again.
workspaces.removedGone: project image {id} was already gone at the provider; its record is removed
workspaces.removedNow: removed project image {id}: its snapshot is gone at the provider, and its record with it
workspaces.noSealedImage: no image yet; run wsp init to build one
workspaces.imageNoVault: no sign-ins held; cut the next version to hold them

catalogNames.build-essential: C toolchain with cmake and ninja

workspaces.addedProject:
{name} {id}: {source} on {computer}, at {path} inside a workspace of it
make one with: wsp new {quoted} "<what you are working on>"
workspaces.noProjectYet: no projects yet; wsp add <folder> records one here, and wsp add <url> --on <computer> records one there. Run wsp add <folder> to record one.
workspaces.nameTheProject: name the project this work is on: {names}. Run wsp projects to read them.
workspaces.copyTakesNone: a workspace of {project} on this computer is a copy of its folder and forks nothing, so it takes no {words}. Drop them.
workspaces.sizeRefused: {word} is not a size this provider offers; the sizes are {sizes}. Name one of those with --size.
workspaces.noProjectImageNamed: no project image named {ref}; wsp snapshot <workspace> takes one
workspaces.projectImageOfOther: {ref} is a project image of {carried}, and this workspace is for {project}. Name a project image of {project}, or run wsp add to record {carried} as a project.
workspaces.cwdNotAbsolute: --cwd is a path on the machine, absolute, and got "{path}". Give a path that opens with /, since whoever reads it works in a folder this line cannot see.
workspaces.leftOne: 1 change left in the workspace; nothing uncommitted travels
workspaces.leftMany: {count} changes left in the workspace; nothing uncommitted travels
workspaces.noDraftBare: no message was drafted: the agent gave none
workspaces.fixConflicts: {name}: asked {agent} to fix the conflicts with {base}
workspaces.fixCheckOrChild: name a failed check or a child to merge, not both
workspaces.postedOne: {name}: review posted on #{number} (1 comment, {folded} in the summary)
workspaces.postedMany: {name}: review posted on #{number} ({count} comments, {folded} in the summary)
